clue.text: It's nearly time for bed

blocks.note: surface reading: someone warning that bedtime is approaching
setter's reading: the period of darkness, when most people sleep

explanation.surface: A parent tells a child that bedtime is coming soon.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like a clock-watching warning; the answer is simply the part of the day in which bedtime falls.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours after sunset are when people normally retire to sleep.

clue.text: Comic trio in Exodus may raise a laugh

definitions.note: a phrase describing what the noun does, rather than a noun

indicators.note: something comic is clownish and disorderly, so the following letters tumble into a new order

blocks.note: all twelve letters of these three words are used

explanation.surface: A three-person comedy routine set during the Israelites' flight from Egypt might get some laughs.
explanation.walkthrough: Nitrous oxide is popularly called laughing gas, which is why it may raise a laugh.
explanation.definitionFit: This anaesthetic gas, nicknamed laughing gas, can make people giggle when inhaled.

clue.text: River Nile - good beat for a boatman

indicators.note: beat as in battered or knocked about, so the letters are knocked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: R is the standard abbreviation for river
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The Nile is a good stretch of river for a boatman to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' sounds like a patrol area on the river, but it tells you to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Venetian oarsman who propels a gondola is a kind of boatman.

clue.text: The roundabout quality

definitions.note: a number is strictly a quantity; the setter stretches 'quality'

indicators.note: round about: the first word goes round the word meaning about

blocks.note: taken as written
re is Latin-derived for concerning or about

explanation.surface: A road junction's character is described in a few words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roundabout' reads as a traffic circle but splits into 'round about'. Three is a number, so 'quality' is a loose stretch by the setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The number after two is a numerical attribute, which the setter loosely calls a quality.

clue.text: Wave for breakfast?

blocks.note: first meaning: to flourish a weapon or object about
second meaning, split in two: a bowl of cereal husks eaten in the morning

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as BRAN DISH to get the breakfast reading; the question mark flags the punning split.
explanation.definitionFit: To flourish something menacingly is to wave it, and a bowl of bran cereal is a morning meal.

clue.text: It's worrying for head of government to be ordered out on call

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter
the word for ordered sits on the outside of the government letter

blocks.note: bade is the past tense of bid, to command
opening letter of government
to ring is to telephone or call

explanation.surface: It is troubling for a prime minister to be sent away when on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered out' reads as dismissed, but 'out' only says the past tense of bid goes outside the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Badgering someone means pestering or harassing them, which is worrying them persistently.

clue.text: Made redundant by a cross editor

blocks.note: taken as written
the letter X is shaped like a cross
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A journalist is sacked by an angry editor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective meaning angry, but it is the letter shaped like a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Axed is informal for dismissed from a job, as when posts are cut.

clue.text: Vehicle is cleared for service

indicators.note: a thing serviced is taken apart and put back together, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: all nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A vehicle has passed inspection and is ready to go back into use.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor car with a compression-ignition engine is a type of vehicle.

clue.text: County of South African prune

blocks.note: SA abbreviates South Africa and South African
to lop is to cut off branches, to prune

explanation.surface: A dried plum from South Africa is said to come from a particular county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prune' looks like the dried fruit but is the verb for trimming. Salop is the old name for Shropshire, an English county bordering Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop is the traditional abbreviated name for Shropshire, an English shire in the West Midlands.

clue.text: Home of 13

blocks.note: surface reading: an address belonging to the answer at 13
setter's reading: the cross-reference is to a famous fictional letter-writer's signature, and this town is where they live

explanation.walkthrough: 'Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells' is the stock British signature for an outraged, conservative writer of letters to newspapers; Tunbridge Wells is a genteel spa town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent spa town is the proverbial residence of the indignant letter-writer who signs off as Disgusted.

clue.text: Mode in which you may be addressed

definitions.text: Mode in which you may be addressed

blocks.clueFragment: Mode in which you may be addressed
blocks.note: surface reading: a manner or style of speaking to someone politely
setter's reading: the pronoun itself is the grammatical form for the one spoken to

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests etiquette or forms of address; the grammar term for the 'you' form is what is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the form of pronouns and verbs referring to the listener, such as you, has this name.

clue.text: Norman bishop met the Queen - it shows how far he went

definitions.text: it shows how far he went

blocks.note: Odo of Bayeux was the Norman bishop, half-brother of William the Conqueror
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A Norman cleric is introduced to the monarch, and something records his journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A mileage-recording instrument in a vehicle measures the distance travelled.

clue.text: Edifice of English bishop

blocks.note: first meaning: a building for worship
second meaning: William, son of Frederick; both were Archbishops of Canterbury with this surname

explanation.surface: A grand building belongs to a churchman in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A temple is a large place of worship, and two Temples, father and son, led the Church of England as archbishops.

clue.text: Like Mandelson, that is a little damp, aired to press

blocks.note: Peter Mandelson was New Labour's famous spin doctor, a master of political presentation
laundry aired before ironing has been dried

explanation.surface: A politician famed for media management is said to be slightly soggy and put out for the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mandelson, a British Labour politician, was nicknamed the Prince of Darkness for his spin-doctoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes whirled in a washing machine's fast cycle come out still slightly moist rather than fully dry.

clue.text: Chap put up with two others, with extreme annoyance

definitions.note: an adverbial phrase standing for an adjective of feeling

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting something up means writing it from bottom to top

blocks.note: Sid is a typical man's name
Gus is another man's name
Ted is a further man's name

explanation.surface: A man lodges with two other men and is extremely annoyed by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two others' supplies two more men's names, Gus and Ted.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disgusted means feeling strong revulsion or outrage, close to extreme annoyance.

clue.text: Maverick daughter isn't holding a party

indicators.note: holding means one word grips another inside it

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written without the apostrophe
a side is a party in a dispute

explanation.surface: A rebellious daughter refuses to host a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The contraction is split open and the party goes in the middle of it, after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissenter who breaks from the official line is an independent-minded rebel, a maverick.

clue.text: Smart circle for entertainment of Marxists

definitions.note: names one entertainer, not entertainment in general

blocks.note: chic means stylish or smart
the letter O is a circle

explanation.surface: A stylish social set puts on a show for left-wing revolutionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marxists' are not communists but the Marx Brothers, the American comedy team.
explanation.definitionFit: Chico Marx was one of the brothers in the famous film comedy act, the piano-playing entertainer.

clue.text: Obstruction that's keeping a politician on the ball

blocks.note: i.e. is Latin id est, meaning that is
MP is a Member of Parliament
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: Something hinders an alert politician who is quick on the uptake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the ball' looks like the idiom for alert, but the ball is a dance. MP goes between I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Impedance is a hindrance or obstruction, from impede, and also electrical resistance.

clue.text: Soldier in sex change - one of the 24

indicators.note: a change alters the order of the letters
in places the soldier inside the other letters

blocks.note: taken as written
RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of soldiers

explanation.surface: A soldier undergoes gender reassignment.
explanation.walkthrough: The 24 is 24 across, fortified wines; Xeres is the old name of Jerez, home of sherry, and of the wine itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Xeres is an archaic name for sherry, a fortified Spanish wine from Jerez.

clue.text: Good parts served to be eaten with garlic

definitions.note: a description of the creature, not a noun

indicators.note: food that is served has been prepared and dished up, so the letters are made over

blocks.note: all nine letters of these two words

explanation.surface: The best cuts of a dish are dished up with garlic.
explanation.walkthrough: Snails, which are gastropods, are eaten in French cooking with garlic butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible snails, cooked as escargots with garlic butter, belong to the mollusc class of slugs and snails.

clue.text: Record goes to American in Olympic event

blocks.note: a record is a gramophone disc
US abbreviates United States, American

explanation.surface: A record is set by an American athlete at the Games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' sounds like a sporting best, but it is a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Throwing a heavy plate for distance is a field contest at the Games.

clue.text: Car turnover achieved by getting publicity about right

indicators.note: turning over flips the order of the letters

blocks.note: ads, advertisements, give publicity
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A car company's sales figures rise thanks to good publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' looks like business revenue but signals reversal. Skoda is a Czech car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: Skoda is a Czech motor manufacturer, so its name stands for one of its cars.

clue.text: Take out girl's deposit

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name, so Di's
to lodge is to deposit, as with money or a complaint

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws the money a young woman put down.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to remove it from its fixed place, to force it out.

clue.text: Many sheep will be found in Sussex

definitions.note: describes a place, not a noun

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, a large number
ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: Plenty of sheep graze in the southern English county of Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewes is the county town of East Sussex, near the sheep-grazing South Downs.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewes is a historic market town located in the county of East Sussex.

clue.text: Old king of note

blocks.note: taken as written
fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch of some renown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of note' reads as 'famous', but it is the word of plus a musical note. Offa was the 8th-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke.
explanation.definitionFit: Offa ruled the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of Mercia in the eighth century.

clue.text: Drinks strengthened damaged sinew

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: fortified means made stronger
taken as written

explanation.surface: Drinks have reinforced a torn tendon.
explanation.definitionFit: Port, sherry and madeira are wines with added spirit, a category of alcoholic drinks.

clue.text: Skill with running water that can be drawn

definitions.note: a description of the object, not a noun

blocks.note: H and C, hot and cold, label the taps of running water
art is skill or craft

explanation.surface: An artist's skill with flowing water makes something worth sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawn' suggests sketching, but here it means pulled along. H and C is the hot-and-cold label in British hotel adverts.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wheeled cart pulled or pushed by hand is something that can be hauled along.

clue.text: Hardback?

blocks.note: first meaning: severe or strict
second meaning: the rear part of a ship
surface padding: the two meanings are printed run together as one word, a bound book

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardback' looks like a bound book, but it splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means harsh or severe, and it also names the rear end of a vessel.
